newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Asbrink says business climate booming.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Asbrink says business climate booming.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday that Sweden's business climate was buoyant and among the world's best.
He also repeated a government pledge to halve unemployment by the year 2000.
"An objective and balanced examination of the total business climate in Sweden shows it is good,", Asbrink said in a written answer to parliamentary questions.
"It is also confirmed by a study which the American chambers of commerce in Europe publicised last autumn," he added.
The U.S. survey named Sweden, Switzerland, Netherlands, Ireland and Israel as having the best business climate in 1996 among 23 compared countries, he said.

"As well as Sweden ranking high when it comes to the total business climate, business leaders gave us high scores when it came to the government's policy toward business, our infrastructure and life quality factors such as hospital care, education and so on," Asbrink said.
He also repeated government pledges to cut unemployment by 50 percent by the year 2000.
"The government is firmly resolved to meet the unemployment aim," Asbrink said.
A rise in unemployment to 8.1 percent in 1996 from 7.7 percent the year before was due to an overall economic slump in several countries during the second half of 1995, Asbrink said.
"A similar development also took place in other countries, not least in Germany with its conservative government," he said. -- Barbara Taltavull, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
